findings.title: Decoder assumes every grant shortcut is exactly two characters
findings.body: The decoder splits the context into fixed two-character fields and requires a six-character prefix, but `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` documents shortcuts as usually three letters and does not enforce a two-character limit. A custom grant using a three-character shortcut can therefore produce an ID during encoding that this decoder rejects or misinterprets, making the token context unreadable. Align the extension contract with the format or support variable-length shortcuts.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher does not verify the grant shortcut
findings.body: This matcher extracts characters 3–4 instead of the grant shortcut at characters 4–5, and returns false when the extracted value equals the expected shortcut. As a result, it does not reliably assert that an event token ID has the expected grant type, so regressions in grant-type encoding can pass these integration assertions.

findings.title: Constructor fails to reject a null raw token ID
findings.body: The second null check checks `grantType` again instead of `rawTokenId`, so a context with a null raw ID is accepted. Encoding that context appends the literal string `null` to the token ID, producing an ID that does not preserve the supplied context and can be mistaken for a real raw ID. Check `rawTokenId` here.
